Here is how I did it in /v/steamsupport:

  1. Go to "flair settings"
  2. Click "Add a new link flair"
  3. Under "flair label" write what you would like the flair to say

  4. Under "Flair CSS class name" type flair-flairname (EXAMPLE)

  5. Go to subverse settings

  6. Add to the custom stylesheet the following

.flair-flairname {

display: inline-block;

background-color: #A80000;

color: white;

}

Life has a tendency to bring us down to a level that is dark, scary, and lonely; and while I don't suggest drinking as a solution to life's problems, I know from personal experience that the social aspects of your local watering hole can be a truly exceptional way to alleviate one's depression, or anxiety.

Several years ago, I was engaged to a guy; and my world was complete. I was happy, I had goals and plans! Unfortunately, I invested my hope in the wrong person. I was cheated on, lied to, and broken by this guy.

At the time, I lived in florida, and just down the road was a local bar - which is where I sought my solace... at first to drown my sorrows, and escape reality. Eventually, however, I found that this place was a refuge for an entirely different reason. My bartender, on top of making sure that I had a full drink in front of me; became a true and loyal friend. He would listen to me, regardless of the subject matter, and contribute honest and genuine advice. He was a shoulder to cry on, and the first source of laughter after my personal darkness. Since then, we've become great friends, we've traveled together, and he has taught me a lot of what I know about bartending; having taken a real interest in me. I'm not saying that every bartender is like this; but the one worth his salt will do a whole lot more than mix a drink or two.

This, to me, is what it means to be a bartender - in addition to the art form itself; it is an opportunity to be a kind face, a warm smile, a listening ear, and a shoulder to cry on. I love what I do, and being able to help people, even in a small way, is the reason that I am proud of what I do.

Tell me your stories, tell us all about the experiences you've had with those great noble night owls, who tend bar, and tend our hearts wounds.

What does your bartender mean to you?
What does your bartender mean to you?

+1 As a bartender and Mixologist in NYC, it's easy to get caught up in the madness of drink-slinging, but I really appreciate those nights being able to relax and chat it up behind the bar and actually listen to my customers. Everyone, kind of like every spirit, is so unique in their development. Plus I love being able to concoct drinks around their stories that may offer some insight to their situation. So yeah, kudos for you rebounding and also shedding light on how valuable bartenders are as people :)

This is a great post. As has been mentioned, far too many people get caught up in the cocktail itself and what is hip at the moment. It's very difficult to distinguish a real bartender from a mixologist. When I'm behind the stick, I find that I (and my guests) have the most fun when I am able to show them something new that they would not have tried at any other bar. To develop their trust is incredibly important to me. We always tell guests to trust us, and if they don't like what we serve them, then we will happily drink it ourselves. To have somebody come in for a second dose of whatever I gave them last time, or to bring a friend with them to discover something new together, is the most rewarding feeling I can get as a bartender. I also make it a point of pride to never keep guests waiting more than is reasonable (we are consistently very busy) and to keep our bar clean and well-stocked. It's hard to respect a sloppy or inattentive bartender.

As a guest at the local watering hole, I try to keep my needs modest. Generally I just want to drink beer, so keeping the glass full is priority #1, because Pacifico can go down faster than water under the right circumstances. It's nice that the barkeep remembers my face and maybe knows my name. We can chat if it's a slower day, but I'll stay out of your way if you're in the shits. Keep it simple.

Cheers!
